function: Learned compensation of five hardware imperfections by designing the digital precoder (Tx) or combiner (Rx) of a THz hybrid-beamforming link to lower SER (pp. 1, 6)
system: 256x256 UM-MIMO with fully connected hybrid beamforming, 4 RF chains, 4 streams, 300 GHz, 1 GHz bandwidth, 50 m; no RIS (pp. 3, 10)
method: Two-stage supervised DNN: sub-NNs (one tanh hidden layer) model the imperfections, then an NN designs the precoder or combiner; MSE loss; pruning, parameter sharing, power-aware slimming (pp. 7-9)
data_channel: Matlab simulation with the multi-ray THz channel model [39] and 16-QAM; 8000 training symbols per stage, 8000 different test symbols; no measured data (p. 10)
test_conditions: Same simulated channel and hardware for training and testing, only new symbols and noise; transmit power swept from -10 to 15 dBm; impairments fixed across both (p. 10)
baselines: Non-learned: ideal hardware and uncompensated 'all errors' system; learned: end-to-end autoencoder [26], D-DNN [33]; Tx versus Rx compensation (p. 11)
metrics: SER uncoded and with convolutional code, constellations, stage-1 approximation error, training loss, number of parameters, running time (pp. 10-13)
complexity: Parameters (Lt+Nt+Lr)(5Nh+2); O(Nh(Lt+Nt+Lr)) and O(Nh(Lt+Lr)); Table II parameter counts and Table III running times (pp. 9, 12, 13)
openness: none; only a demonstration video at https://twclabsjtu.github.io/THz-Imperfect-Hardware/ (p. 14)
q1_support: p. 10: "The multi-ray channel model is used" for THz; the data are simulated, and no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "remain fixed across training and testing" for PA nonlinearity, IQ imbalance and phase noise; the test set is new symbols of the same setup, plus a power sweep.
q3_support: p. 11: "the end-to-end autoencoder" [26] and D-DNN [33] are earlier learned baselines; p. 13: "non-ideal system with D-DNN" and the uncompensated non-ideal system are compared on SER.
q4_support: p. 13: "computational complexity of these two combined methods is" O(Nh(Lt+Nt+Lr)) and O(Nh(Lt+Lr)), with parameter counts (Table II) and running times (Table III).
q5_support: p. 14: "The demonstration video can be found" at a lab website; it is a video, not code or data, and the training data are simulated (p. 10).
notes: Borderline function: compensation of hardware imperfections resembles amplifier linearization, but it covers DAC/ADC, IQ imbalance, phase noise, phase shifters and PA, and the learned output is the digital precoder or combiner of hybrid beamforming (p. 6), so area 3. q3 non-learned baseline is the uncompensated 'With all errors' curve of Fig. 7(c) (p. 11), a do-nothing baseline. Real THz measurements are only future work (p. 14).
